hook: I want developers to run five agents and still feel calm

builtFor.context: cmux is where developers run many AI coding agents at once. As agent count grows, the scarce resource is the developer's attention.

opportunities.title: Attention Queue
opportunities.body: Who needs you, why, and how long they've waited.

opportunities.title: Answer inline
opportunities.body: Allow once, reply or open the pane, without switching.

opportunities.title: Protect flow
opportunities.body: Keyboard-first, oldest first, quiet when clear.

body: I run AI agents every day to prototype in code, which is how I built this concept, so I design cmux's problems as a user.
My product work has been in trust-heavy tools where people act on what a system raises: transaction monitoring at Youverify.

bring.title: Trust in automated systems
bring.body: Tools where people act on what a system flagged and know when to step in.

bring.title: Design systems
bring.body: A component library that cut developer onboarding by 45%.

bring.title: AI-assisted prototyping
bring.body: Working prototypes in code, like this one.

systemsGets: Someone obsessed with the 1px details and the states between human and agent (working, waiting, blocked, done).

opportunity.title: Attention Queue
opportunity.problem: Pane rings show where an agent needs you, not why, so every request means switching panes and reading back.
opportunity.solution: A queue labelled by why each agent waits, with inline answers, oldest first, and an all-clear state.

firstWeek.intro: My first week would be dogfooding cmux hard and shipping one improvement.

days.body: Set up cmux with five agents on real work. Note every friction.
Read issues and community feedback; talk to heavy users.
Pick one interaction to improve with the founders.
Prototype it in code against the real app.
Ship it, or open the PR, and share what changed.

ask: I'd love to be cmux's founding designer.
